messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Reactives more excitable -
parts:
Hi, This has probably been covered, but use a trick to prevent dynamic UI from being re-rendered each time the user selects something from a drop-down:

The user selects one or two strings from the drop-down
I render different tabs for 'one' vs 'two'
the actual strings can change while still being only one of them (or two of them).

e.g. the user selected Jan, or Feb or March etc. 
or the user selected Jan AND Feb or Jan AND March.

I created a function like this :

countMonths <- reactive(function() {
  length(input$months)
})

And thus the reactive UI stays the same unless the user decides to select MORE (1->2) or LESS (2->1) months.

This works because reactives cache their result, and if it's still the same, then the parent function is not triggered.

If I replace the call to countMonths() with a number (e.g. 1) in my reactive UI function, then the reactive UI (correctly) doesn't update.
If I replace the contents of countMonths with just return(1) then the reactive UI (correctly) doesn't update.

However, this no longer seems to work - each time the user moves from Jan->Feb, the reactive UI gets re-run and blows away my tab position (not to mention rendering the output twice - once for the month update and then again to move to the default tab).

I did update shiny from CRAN yesterday but I don't know if that's the issue.

Does this seem familiar?  

Is there some way I can see why shiny decides to re-trigger the reactiveUI function?

Does the new lazy work fix this?  

Why did I think it used to work?

-Alex

Is this related to the move to lazy functions?  Is that even on CRAN yet?

Obviously if countMonths is lazily evaluated then shiny can't tell if it's worth executing reactiveUI function before it calls the reactiveUI function (which calls countMonths), when it's too late.

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Reactives more excitable -
parts:
Hi Alex,

It is related to the reactive-function-lazy-evaluation change. The property you are describing, let's call "insulation". Shiny reactive funcs used to have insulation but not laziness. Now they have laziness but not insulation.  However, there is a different technique you can use now to get insulation. 

v <- reactiveValues(countMonths=0)
observe(function() {
  v$countMonths <- length(input$months)
})

From your reactiveUI, use v$countMonths to read the value instead of countMonths().

Essentially, observe provides the eagerness and going through reactiveValues provides the insulation.
On Friday, February 8, 2013, Alex Brown wrote:

Is this related to the move to lazy functions?  Is that even on CRAN yet?

Obviously if countMonths is lazily evaluated then shiny can't tell if it's worth executing reactiveUI function before it calls the reactiveUI function (which calls countMonths), when it's too late.

-Alex
